title: Statins inhibit Rho kinase activity in patients with atherosclerosis
authors: Nohria A, Prsic A, Liu PY, Okamoto R, Creager MA, Selwyn A, et al.
population: Patients with stable atherosclerosis randomised to atorvastatin 80 mg, atorvastatin 10 mg or placebo
funder: This work was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health (HL052233, PO1 HL-48743); Doris Duke Charitable Foundation; and Pfizer, Inc. (Morristown, NJ). One author received a National Health Research Institute grant from Taiwan.
result: Atorvastatin 80 mg reduced leukocyte Rho kinase (ROCK) activity against placebo (p = 0.002), significantly within 2 weeks, and the reduction remained after controlling for changes in LDL cholesterol and triglycerides (p = 0.01); changes in ROCK activity did not correlate with changes in LDL cholesterol (r = 0.2, p = 0.25). Rho activation requires isoprenoid intermediates of the mevalonate pathway. The authors describe these as first-in-man findings.
